summary: The PASTEUR Act of 2026 establishes a program within the Department of Health and Human Services to encourage the development of innovative antimicrobial drugs that target challenging, high-threat pathogens. It creates subscription-style contracts for eligible antimicrobial drugs, provides grants for health facilities and outpatient settings to promote appropriate antibiotic use, and appropriates $6,000,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 to carry out these efforts.

affected_groups.effect: May apply for U.S. novel antimicrobial supply contracts, receive annual subscription payments between $75,000,000 and $300,000,000, and must adhere to specific manufacturing, supply, and reporting requirements.

Eligible for grant funding to support the judicious use of antimicrobial drugs, establish stewardship programs, and participate in surveillance networks, with prioritization for rural, tribal, and safety-net hospitals.
Eligible to receive pilot program grants for implementing or expanding outpatient antibiotic stewardship programs, with a priority on urgent care settings and retail health clinics.
Expected to benefit from improved commercial availability and research into innovative medicines targeting severe and life-threatening infections.

key_provisions: Establishes a contract program where the Secretary can enter into agreements with sponsors of eligible antimicrobial drugs that treat urgent or serious threats.

Creates a quantitative scoring methodology and minimum scoring threshold for evaluating eligible antimicrobial applications based on patient care contributions, innovative characteristics, and public health benefits.
Requires contract recipients to ensure commercial availability, maintain sufficient drug supplies, track and report drug resistance data, and follow appropriate-use and manufacturing best practices.
Provides annual subscription payments ranging from $75,000,000 to $300,000,000 per contract, adjusted for inflation and domestic net sales revenue, for a term of up to 10 years.
Establishes the Critical Need Antimicrobial Advisory Group composed of 15 members to advise on scoring criteria and pathogen prioritization.
Creates a grant program for hospitals, nursing facilities, and outpatient care settings to implement and expand antibiotic stewardship programs and resistance surveillance.
Appropriates $6,000,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 to remain available until expended, designating up to 6.5 percent of those funds for the grant and surveillance programs.
missing_information: Specific details regarding the exact regulatory weights that will be assigned within the scoring methodology categories, as those are directed to be promulgated post-enactment.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The PASTEUR Act of 2026 establishes a program within the Department of Health and Human Services to encourage the development of innovative antimicrobial drugs that target challenging, high-threat pathogens. It creates subscription-style contracts for eligible antimicrobial drugs, provides grants for health facilities and outpatient settings to promote appropriate antibiotic use, and appropriates $6,000,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 to carry out these efforts.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a federal financial framework committing $6 billion to incentivize the commercial development and supply of novel antibiotics while funding health facility stewardship and resistance surveillance.
